era_en: Sengoku Period to Early Edo Period (1543-1616)
school: 日本德川幕府/关东集团
historical_significance: 德川家康（1543-1616），日本战国时代末期的军事将领和政治家，日本三大统一者之一。他在桶狭间之战中生存， later 通过山崎、小关、德川家康等战役消灭竞争对手。1600年关原之战中击败石田三长，统一日本。1603年建立德川幕府，成为征夷大将军，将Capital迁至江户（现东京），建立历时265年的幕府政治。他颁布Kinchu Narabani Kuge Shohatto、Buke Shohatto和一国一城令等法令，控制大名，确立封建领主体系。晚年将职位传给儿子德川秀忠，但仍实际上控制政权。他的统治带来了‘江户时代’两百五十年的和平与稳定，日本实现了国家统一、经济复兴和文化繁荣。他还积极推行外交贸易，与东南亚国家保持关系，同时严格管控基督教传入。
historical_significance_en: Tokugawa Ieyasu (1543-1616), one of the three great unifiers of Japan, was a military leader and politician during the late Sengoku period. Surviving the Battle of Okehazama, he later eliminated rivals through battles at Yamazaki, Kotsu, and others. In the Battle of Sekigahara in 1600, he defeated Ishida Mitsunari and unified Japan. In 1603, he established the Tokugawa Shogunate, becoming Seii Taishogun, and moved the capital to Edo (modern Tokyo), establishing a shogunate government lasting 265 years. He enacted Kinchu Narabani Kuge Shohatto, Buke Shohatto and the One Castle per Province decree to control daimyo and establish the feudal domain system. In his later years, he passed the position to his son Tokugawa Iemitsu, but continued to rule behind the scenes. His reign brought 'Edo period' peace and stability for 250 years, during which Japan achieved national unification, economic revival, and cultural prosperity. He also actively promoted diplomacy and trade, maintaining relations with Southeast Asian countries while strictly controlling the introduction of Christianity.

cross_references.relation_type: 权力传承对照：德川 vs 织田
cross_references.description_zh: 德川家康原为织田军下属，后通过关原之战夺取全国统一权力，形成逆袭式的权力转移：织田 Nobunaga 统一日本大部后被丰臣 Hideyoshi 征服，而德川家康最终在关原之战中击败石田三长，确立 Tokugawa 统治。此对比展示了日本战国时期权力传承的多种可能性与不确定性。
cross_references.description_en: Tokugawa Ieyasu originally served under Oda forces, then seized nationwide power through the Battle of Sekigahara, forming an 'upset' power transfer: After Oda Nobunaga unified much of Japan, he was conquered by Toyotomi Hideyoshi, while Tokugawa Ieyasu ultimately defeated Ishida Mitsunari at the Battle of Sekigahara, establishing Tokugawa rule. This contrast shows the various possibilities and uncertainties of power succession in Japan's Sengoku period.

cross_references.relation_type: 君民关系反向：水舟论 vs 德川家康的治理哲学
cross_references.description_zh: 德川家康的'一国一城令'与黄宗羲的'天下为主君为客'形成有趣的历史呼应：前者从政治角度限制大名兵力以维持政权稳定，后者从政治哲学角度颠覆君权合法性（人民是主体）。德川的治理是工具性的民本，黄宗羲的民本是本体性的。二者均承认民众在政治体系中的核心地位，但出发点与逻辑不同。
cross_references.description_en: The 'One Castle per Province' decree of Tokugawa Ieyasu and Huang Zongxi's 'Tianxia is principal, ruler is guest' form an interesting historical echo: the former restricts daimyo military power from a political perspective to maintain regime stability, while the latter subverts imperial legitimacy from a philosophical angle (the people are the subject). Tokugawa's governance is instrumental populism; Huang's is ontological populism. Both acknowledge the central position of the populace in the political system, but differ in their starting points and logic.

cross_references.relation_type: 水舟辩证法对照：李世民 vs 德川家康
cross_references.description_zh: 李世民的'水舟论'与德川家康的'一国一城令'形成有趣的历史呼应：前者从民心承载政权的角度认识民众力量的双重性，后者从政治角度通过限制大名兵力来维持政权稳定。二者均认可民众力量的决定性作用，但干预手段不同。
cross_references.description_en: Li Shimin's 'water-boat theory' and Tokugawa Ieyasu's 'One Castle per Province decree' form an interesting historical echo: the former recognizes the dual nature of popular power from the perspective of regime sustainability, while the latter directly controls military power through institutional arrangement. Both recognize the decisive role of popular power, but differ in their intervention methods.
